turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Nice to be here. I'm doing alright, thanks for having me.
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Uh, around 11:40, so pretty late. Had a closing shift so that's about normal for me."
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?
"About six hours, I'd say. It was okay, not great — I woke up around 3, couldn't shut my brain off about a route change at work, so that ate into things a bit before I got back down."
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?

"Honestly, just watched a little TV, some late-night show, nothing special. I don't have much of a wind-down routine — by the time I'm off shift I'm just trying to relax for a few minutes before I crash."
Thanks for explaining that. Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

"Honestly probably the shift changes more than anything. Bouncing between the early and the late week throws my body off, and then work stuff — like this route reschedule — creeps into my head at night. The street noise doesn't help either, but I'm pretty used to that by now."
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your shifts or how much work follows you home at night?

"Yeah, pretty typical honestly — the shift bouncing's been going on for a while, that's just the job. This particular thing with the route was more of a one-off headache, not something that usually follows me home. Most nights it's just the noise or the schedule messing with me, not actual work stuff replaying in my head."
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

"Eh, it's fine — I wouldn't say I'm losing sleep over it, pun intended. It's just the nature of rotating shifts, so I don't really expect it to be great, and I'm functional enough to do my job, so I'm not gonna complain too much."
Thanks, that makes sense. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

"Seven to nine? Yeah, right, when? No, honestly, not really practical on this schedule — maybe on my off days I get close, but with the shift bouncing around, six or so is more the reality. I don't beat myself up over it, it just is what it is."
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

"Honestly, the shift bouncing is the biggest thing working against me — my body never gets a chance to settle into a rhythm before it flips again. What makes it easier, I guess, is just being tired enough that I fall asleep fast even when the schedule's a mess. It's more about surviving the swap than actually fixing it."
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

"Not really, no — I'm pretty wiped by the time I get in bed, so scrolling doesn't hold much appeal. Might glance at texts from my daughter if she's sent something, but that's about it before the lights go off."
Thanks for sharing that. Do you regularly use social media at all? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
"Nah, not really — I've got the daughter's Facebook to check in on every now and then, that's about it. I'm not really doom-scrolling Instagram or whatever before bed, doesn't interest me much."
Thanks, that’s clear. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
"Nah, can't say I do — my daughter's tried to get me to mess with one, but it's not really my thing. I'll take a phone call over typing at a robot any day."
Got it, thanks. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
"Honestly, staying on one shift long enough for my body to figure out what time zone it's in — the flipping back and forth is the real problem, not the total hours."
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that kind of stable shift would be doable for you? Why or why not?

"Nah, not really — I don't see it happening. Logistics doesn't work that way, somebody's got to cover the early and late ends, and with seniority the way it is I don't get first pick. Learned to just roll with it at this point."

Thanks for explaining that. Now I have a few background questions. You can skip anything you’d rather not share.

Your age?
Thank you. What’s your profession?
Warehouse logistics coordinator — I schedule and track deliveries, that sort of thing.
Thanks. What country were you born in?
I was born in the U.S. — grew up in a small town, moved here about eight years back for the job.
Thanks. And which country do you currently live in?
"United States."

Thanks, that’s all the main questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else you’d like to add about your sleep, your schedule, or anything we talked about today?
